versos.texto_bv: O santuário tinha um umbral quadrado; e a face do santo dos santos tinha a mesma aparência que a do santuário.
versos.traducao_literal: O santuário, umbral quadrado; e face do santo: a aparência como a aparência.
objecoes: Objeção MATERIAL (revisão ER-0019): A expansão 'tinha a mesma aparência que a do santuário' fecha dentro do v. 21 a elipse hebraica 'a aparência como a aparência', enquanto NTLH, ARA e NVIPT ligam a comparação ao altar de madeira do v. 22; corrigir o referente da comparação exigiria mudar o sentido, o que é vedado à revisão editorial. — evidência: traducao_literal: 'e face do santo: a aparência como a aparência'; NTLH: 'havia uma coisa que parecia' (→ altar, v. 22); ARA: 'diante do santuário havia uma coisa semelhante' (→ altar); NVIPT: 'o que ficava em frente do Lugar Santíssimo era semelhante'. RAT-1 (ratio 1.62) flagra exatamente essa expansão interpretativa.

kjv.texto: The posts of the temple were squared, and the face of the sanctuary; the appearance of the one as the appearance of the other.

vizinhos.20: From the ground unto above the door were cherubims and palm trees made, and on the wall of the temple.
vizinhos.22: The altar of wood was three cubits high, and the length thereof two cubits; and the corners thereof, and the length thereof, and the walls thereof, were of wood: and he said unto me, This is the table that is before the Lord.

web.texto: As for the temple, the door posts were squared; and as for the face of the sanctuary, its appearance was as the appearance of the temple.

vizinhos.20: from the ground to above the door were cherubim and palm trees made: thus was the wall of the temple.
vizinhos.22: The altar was of wood, three cubits high, and its length two cubits; and its corners, and its length, and its walls, were of wood: and he said to me, This is the table that is before Yahweh.

versos.texto_bv: E as câmaras laterais estavam dispostas uma junto à outra, trinta e três vezes; havia rebaixos na parede da casa, ao redor, destinados a sustentar as câmaras laterais, para que ficassem apoiadas ali — e não ficassem encaixadas na própria parede da casa.
versos.traducao_literal: E as câmaras laterais, câmara em direção a câmara, trinta e três vezes; e entravam na parede que [pertencia] à casa, para as câmaras laterais, ao redor, ao redor, para serem seguras; e não seriam seguras na parede da casa.
objecoes: Objeção MATERIAL (revisão ER-0019): A BV lê 'trinta e três vezes' (33) onde as três referências leem três andares com trinta câmaras em cada (3×30); alinhar com NTLH/ARA/NVIPT exigiria mudança de sentido numérico, vedada à revisão editorial. — evidência: traducao_literal: 'câmara em direção a câmara, trinta e três vezes'; NTLH: 'três andares, trinta cômodos em cada andar'; ARA: 'três andares… e trinta em cada andar'; NVIPT: 'três andares, havendo trinta em cada andar'. O heb. 'shalosh u-shloshim pe'amim' admite as duas leituras; a adjudicação é material, não de forma.

kjv.texto: And the side chambers were three, one over another, and thirty in order; and they entered into the wall which was of the house for the side chambers round about, that they might have hold, but they had not hold in the wall of the house.

vizinhos.5: After he measured the wall of the house, six cubits; and the breadth of every side chamber, four cubits, round about the house on every side.
vizinhos.7: And there was an enlarging, and a winding about still upward to the side chambers: for the winding about of the house went still upward round about the house: therefore the breadth of the house was still upward, and so increased from the lowest chamber to the highest by the midst.

web.texto: The side rooms were in three stories, one over another, and thirty in order; and they entered into the wall which belonged to the house for the side rooms all around, that they might be supported, and not penetrate the wall of the house.

vizinhos.5: Then he measured the wall of the house, six cubits; and the breadth of every side room, four cubits, all around the house on every side.
vizinhos.7: The side rooms were wider on the higher levels, because the walls were narrower at the higher levels. Therefore the breadth of the house increased upward; and so one went up from the lowest level to the highest through the middle level.
